original_question: Does there exist an infinite family of semigroup conjugacy relations that are first-order definable, that agree with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, and that form an antichain under inclusion, so that no one of the relations contains another?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.21 from Araujo-Kinyon-Konieczny-Malheiro, as restated in Section 1 and again in Section 7 of arXiv:2411.16284, specifically the antichain branch: whether there exists an infinite set of first-order definable semigroup conjugacies forming an antichain under inclusion.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right open problem branch from Section 1 and Section 7: it asks for infinitely many first-order definable semigroup conjugacies, requires agreement with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, and asks for pairwise noncontainment rather than a chain. Those are the essential ingredients of the antichain half of Problem 6.21.
missing_details: The paper's term "semigroup conjugacy" is not just any relation agreeing with group conjugacy on groups; it is an equivalence relation with that property, so the question should say this explicitly to be fully stand-alone (Section 2).

The order relation is the global inclusion order on conjugacies: rho is contained in sigma if, for every semigroup for which they are defined and every pair of elements a,b, a rho b implies a sigma b (Section 2).
The word "antichain" should be unpacked as pairwise incomparability with respect to that inclusion order, not merely "different" or "non-equal" relations (Section 2; Section 7).

The scope is unrestricted semigroups; the problem is not limited to finite semigroups, inverse semigroups, epigroups, cancellative semigroups, or semigroups embeddable in groups (Section 1; Section 7).

To stay paper-faithful, the question must remain about conjugacies, not merely first-order definable relations that agree with group conjugacy on groups, because Section 8 constructs weaker first-order definable relations of that kind that are not transitive in general.
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite set of first-order definable semigroup conjugacies {rho_i : i in I} such that, for every group G, each rho_i coincides with ordinary group conjugacy on G, and for any distinct i,j in I neither rho_i is contained in rho_j nor rho_j is contained in rho_i, where containment of conjugacies means: for every semigroup S and all a,b in S, if a is rho_i-conjugate to b in S, then a is rho_j-conjugate to b in S?
justification: This is the antichain half of Problem 6.21 as restated in the introduction and at the start of Section 7. Section 2 provides the formal meanings of both "semigroup conjugacy" and the inclusion order on conjugacies, which are the only substantive details your draft leaves implicit. The paper answers only the chain half by constructing an infinite chain in Theorem 7.1, while Section 8 shows that one can also build first-order definable relations agreeing with group conjugacy on groups that are not conjugacies in general, so the refined question should remain explicitly at the level of conjugacies.
